claims.claim: He was born around 315–320 near Eleutheropolis in Palestine and died at sea in May 403.
The controversy surrounding the letter concerned the legitimacy of religious images, a debate that later became central to the Byzantine Iconoclast Controversy of the 8th–9th centuries.
Epiphanius claimed that in 394 he personally saw a newly made Christian image, destroyed it, and then appealed to imperial authority because leading bishops were tolerant of such images.
Later legal and theological disputes cited the letter as proof of early anti‑iconic sentiment, influencing arguments of Byzantine iconoclasts.
Modern scholars debate the authenticity of the letter, with some suggesting it may be a later forgery, yet it remains a key source for understanding fourth‑century attitudes toward images.
